scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. I'm 33 years old and have been living with my parents most of my life. They charge me $200, which seems reasonable given where we live. I pay rent, which helps, but I'm still living with them. We mostly get along, but I tend to avoid them a lot. Recently, there was a plumbing issue in my bathroom, so they had to remodel my section of the house. This means we're running into each other more often than before, which has probably increased the chances of conflict. Today, my parents went to Costco. When they got home, I was sitting on the couch playing Apex Legends. My mom asked me to help bring in the groceries, and I told her I'd do it in a minute. I was too engrossed in my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get my ass up, and I again said I'd do it in a minute. He got frustrated, grabbed the controller out of my hand, and it turned into a huge shouting match. Now, they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which seems impossible. They also brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They're comparing me to him, which I find really unfair. I mean, I could have gotten up and helped them, but since I pay rent, I feel like I have the right to say no when they ask for help with groceries or yardwork. Am I the asshole here? Alright, let's break this down. First, I'm living with my parents, paying rent, which seems fair. I'm an adult, so I should be contributing more, but I'm already paying rent. They're asking me to help with groceries, which is a reasonable request. However, I was playing a game and didn't want to stop. I told them I'd help in a minute, but they got frustrated because I didn't act immediately. I can see why they got upset. They probably felt that I wasn't respecting their request or that I was being selfish by continuing to play the game instead of helping out. On the other hand, I feel like I'm contributing financially, and I should have the right to have some downtime or leisure time without being interrupted. The comparison to my younger brother adds another layer of frustration. It seems like they're using him as an example of what I should be doing, which is unfair because everyone's situation is different. My brother is married, has kids, and has a stable job, which is great, but it doesn't mean I'm not contributing in my own way. The shouting match escalated things, and now they're checking into a hotel, expecting me to find a place by Friday. That seems extreme, especially since finding a place to live in a short time frame is difficult. It makes me feel like they're trying to force me out, which is stressful. I wonder if there's a middle ground here. Maybe I could have paused the game and helped them, showing that I'm willing to contribute even though I'm paying rent. It might have prevented the argument from escalating. On the other hand, I was already contributing financially, so I might feel like I'm doing my part, and they should respect that. I also think about the dynamic of living with parents as an adult. It's a delicate balance between contributing financially and emotionally supporting the family. It seems like there's a lack of communication here. Instead of getting frustrated, maybe we could have talked about how to handle these situations better in the future. Overall, I feel like both sides have valid points. I was being asked to help with a reasonable request, and I was unresponsive, which led to frustration. However, I also feel like I'm contributing in my own way by paying rent, and I should have some autonomy over my time. The comparison to my brother and the sudden demand to find a place by Friday are adding to the tension. Maybe the best approach is to communicate openly about expectations. I could explain that I feel like I'm contributing financially and that I need some downtime, while they could express their feelings about needing help around the house. Finding a balance where both sides feel respected and heard could help prevent future conflicts. In the end, I don't think I'm entirely the asshole, but I could have handled the situation better by being more responsive and showing willingness to help, even if it's not my primary responsibility. Communication is key in these situations to avoid misunderstandings and escalate tensions.
